## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics and NULL documentation should be corrected because they misrepresent started processes and processes with earlier start events.

## Changes
The pull request adds `finished_at` to the latest-event process model and documents it in the schema catalog, preserving one row per process. It also adds `review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Started processes receive a finish timestamp — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, the model returns a finish timestamp without a completion event. The predicate `event_type = 'started'` selects its start time, contradicting the catalog's “Timestamp when the process finished.” — Consumers using `finished_at` to identify completed processes will treat a process that has only started as finished.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — For process 30, a `started` event followed by `cleared` produces NULL despite its start history. “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`, which examines only the latest event. — Consumers following this description will misclassify previously started processes after a subsequent `cleared` event.
